_comment: Actions with a documented supply-chain compromise. Per-entry fields: tags_hijacked (tag/branch refs are CRITICAL), compromised_shas (confirmed malicious commits, CRITICAL even when pinned), safe_shas (vendor-confirmed clean commits, INFO), any_ref_critical (no known-safe ref exists, so every ref is CRITICAL). A pinned SHA that appears in neither list is MEDIUM: verify it predates the incident. Compromised actions have been re-enabled still containing malicious code (actions-cool, Sept 2026), so entries are never removed after a takedown.

actions.summary: Mutable version tags were force-moved to a malicious commit that dumped CI runner memory (including secrets) to workflow logs.
Compromised as part of the same campaign that hit tj-actions/changed-files; also had a tag force-moved to malicious code.
75 of 76 version tags were force-pushed to malicious commits carrying a credential stealer that read Runner.Worker memory. Tags were restored after about 12 hours.

All 7 tags (v0.2.0 to v0.2.6) were force-pushed to malicious commits in the same attack as trivy-action. It is also pulled in internally by trivy-action, so SHA-pinning only the outer action did not always protect users.
All 35 version tags were force-pushed to malicious commits that ran a rogue setup.sh payload. Vendor guidance is to move to v2.1.20 or newer.
Version v2.3.28 was confirmed compromised in the same campaign as the KICS action.

Every tag was moved to an imposter commit that downloaded Bun, read Runner.Worker memory and sent credentials to an attacker domain. The repository was re-enabled on 2026-09-16 still containing the malicious code and had to be disabled a second time.
15 tags were moved to malicious commits with the same payload as issues-helper. Also re-enabled in September 2026 with the malicious code still present.
A malicious commit was force-pushed and several version tags were redirected to it, so any workflow running those tags afterwards executed the attacker's payload in the runner.
